rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.panov.l1: The c4-pawn captures on d5. With no pawn on the c- and e-files, the white d4-pawn is now isolated.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.panov.l2: The knight recaptures on d5, the square in front of the isolated pawn. No white pawn can attack it there, and it blocks the pawn.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.panov.l3: What White gets in return: the c- and e-files without a white pawn, for the rooks, and the e5-square for the knight, supported by the d4-pawn.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.panov.l4: With many pieces on the board, the isolated pawn gives space and activity. When pieces are traded and the endgame nears, it becomes a target: the position decides.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.panov.l5: Two neighbouring pawns side by side, with no pawns of their colour on the files next to them, are hanging pawns. No pawn defends them, and when one is traded, the other becomes isolated.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.panov.e1: Attack: an isolated pawn has no pawns of its own colour on the neighbouring files. No pawn can defend it: only the pieces protect it.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.panov.e2: This is the Caro-Kann Defence, Panov Attack. White has pawns on c4 and d4 and no longer has the e-pawn.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.p: Find the move that captures the isolated pawn.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.certo: The rook captures the d5-pawn. If the white queen recaptures, the b3-bishop takes it, with the d7-queen in reserve.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.revela: The rook captures the d5-pawn: three attackers against two defenders, and if the white queen recaptures, the b3-bishop takes it.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.err.b3d1.1: The bishop captures the d1-bishop, but leaves the diagonal that attacked the d5-pawn.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.err.b3d1.2: The rook recaptures. Now it is two attackers against two defenders, and the d5-pawn holds.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.err.b3d1.3: Back to the position: count the attackers and defenders of the d5-pawn and capture it.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.err.b3d5.1: The bishop captures the d5-pawn, but stands in front of the black rook and queen on the d-file.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.err.b3d5.2: The white bishop goes to f3 and attacks the one on d5. If the black bishop takes on f3, the d-file opens and the white queen captures the d6-rook.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.err.b3d5.3: Back to the position: capture the d5-pawn with the piece that keeps the b3-bishop in reserve.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.fora: That move does not attack the d5-pawn. Use one of the black pieces that already attack it.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.volta: Try again: capture the isolated pawn.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.e1: Attack: now let's think from Black's side, against White's isolated pawn. This position comes from a game played on Lichess, close to the endgame.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.e2: Black attacks the d5-pawn with the rook on d6, the queen on d7 behind it and the bishop on b3. White defends it only with the queen on d4 and the rook on d2.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.l0: On d5, the rook is defended by the b3-bishop and the d7-queen.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.l1: Attacked by the rook, the white queen captures on d5.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.l2: The bishop recaptures. Black gave the rook but won the pawn and the queen: Black has the queen against a rook.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.l3: In endgames like this, count the attackers and defenders of the isolated pawn. With more attackers, it falls, because no neighbouring pawn can come to defend it.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.contra.l4: In the count, a defender pinned to the king usually does not count: off the line of the pin, it cannot recapture.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.proprio.p: Find the move that uses the isolated pawn to clear the way for the queen.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.proprio.certo: The pawn advances to d6 and opens the diagonal: the queen attacks the a8-rook, and the pawn attacks the e7-knight and the c7-pawn.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.proprio.revela: The pawn advances to d6: the queen's diagonal to the a8-rook opens, and the pawn also attacks the e7-knight and the c7-pawn.
The queen captures the e7-knight with check, but no white piece defends it there.
The king recaptures the queen. White gave the queen for a knight.
Back to the position: look for a move of the d5-pawn.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.proprio.fora: That move does not use the d5-pawn. Look for a move by it or by the e4-queen.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.proprio.e1: Attack: White again, now with the isolated pawn on your side. This position comes from a French Defence played on Lichess.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.proprio.e2: The queen on e4 and the rook on a8 are on the same diagonal, but the isolated d5-pawn stands between them.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.proprio.l0: Now White threatens to capture the a8-rook with the queen and the e7-knight with the pawn.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.proprio.l1: The c7-pawn captures on d6, and the diagonal between the queen and the a8-rook is clear.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.proprio.l2: The queen captures the a8-rook. White gave the isolated pawn and won a rook.
rot.isolatedPawn.ideia.proprio.l3: With the pieces on the board, the isolated pawn also attacks: here it did not wait to be surrounded and advanced to open the queen's diagonal.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra.l.2: The bishop captures the d4-pawn with check. By leaving f6, it opens the rank, and the g6-queen attacks the e6-queen.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra.l.3: White blocks the check with the bishop on e3.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra.l.4: The black queen captures the e6-queen.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra.l.5: The e3-bishop recaptures on d4. Black gave the bishop and won the queen.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra.l.6: Without a neighbouring pawn to defend it, the isolated pawn depends on the pieces. Here none defended it, and the bishop captured it with check.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra.1: Attack demonstration: now let's think from Black's side. This position comes from a game played on Lichess. White's d4-pawn is isolated and undefended.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra2.l.3: The c5-pawn captures on d4 with check.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra2.l.4: The king recaptures. The c4-pawn is now isolated, and the king is on d4, on the same diagonal as the e5-knight.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra2.l.5: The bishop goes to f6 and pins the e5-knight to the king. The knight cannot move, and the black king also attacks it: Black wins the knight.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra2.l.6: Here the trade on d4 broke up the pair: the c4-pawn was left isolated, and the white king, recapturing, landed on the bishop's diagonal. Before attacking hanging pawns, see what trading one of them leaves behind.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra2.1: Attack demonstration: Black again, in another Lichess game. White has hanging pawns on c4 and d4: side by side, with no white pawns on the b- and e-files.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.regra2.2: Like the isolated pawn, hanging pawns have no pawn to defend them. When one of them is traded, the other becomes isolated.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.excecao.l.2: The d4-pawn advances to d5 and attacks the c6-queen. On d5 it cuts the diagonal that linked the queen to the f3-rook.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.excecao.l.3: The e6-pawn captures on d5 and saves the queen, but the black pawn on d5 still cuts the diagonal.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.excecao.l.4: The queen captures the f3-rook, which was left undefended.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.excecao.l.5: Hanging pawns also attack: here the advance of one of them cut the rook's defence. Before judging them a target, see whether an advance settles it: the position decides.
rot.isolatedPawn.demos.excecao.1: Attack demonstration: White again, now with the hanging pawns on your side, on c4 and d4. The c6-queen defends the f3-rook along the diagonal.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.alvo.enunciado: White has an isolated pawn. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.alvo.fim: The queen captured the isolated pawn with check and, at the same time, attacked the b4-bishop. The king got out of check, and the queen captured the bishop.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.alvo.err.d3e3: 28...Qe3+? is check, but captures nothing. After 29.Kh1, the queen on d4 would no longer give check, and White is better.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.pendentes.enunc: Black has hanging pawns. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.pendentes.fim: The queen captured the d5-pawn with check and attacked the e4-knight. The bishop blocked the check on e6 and cut the e8-rook's defence, and the queen captured the knight.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.pendentes.err.h: 25.Qh6? captures nothing: 25...Bg7 attacks the queen, and Black takes the advantage.
25.Qd1? retreats the queen without capturing anything: 25...Nxc3 captures a pawn and attacks the queen, and Black is better.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.pendentes.err2: 26.Qxe6+? gives the queen for the bishop: after 26...Rxe6, even capturing the e4-knight, White has bishop and knight for the queen, and the advantage is gone.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.proprio.enuncia: Your d4-pawn is isolated. Is it only a weakness here, or can it help the attack? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.proprio.fim: The isolated pawn advanced and opened the queen's diagonal to the king: it was check. The black queen blocked on f6, stopped defending the a5-rook, and the white queen captured it.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.proprio.err.c3c: 24.Qxc6? wins a pawn, but the queen leaves the black king's diagonal, and the check by the pawn advance is gone. The position is equal.
rot.isolatedPawn.pratica.proprio.err2: 25.dxc6? captures the pawn, but 25...Qxc3 trades queens and the a5-rook is saved: Black is better.
